paper.title: Distributed algorithms for learning and cognitive medium access with logarithmic regret

settings.name_in_paper: Distributed learning and access with known number of secondary users
unmapped: U <= C players (secondary users) each select one of C channels per slot without communication; colliding transmissions all fail
each player observes the channel availability (sensing) regardless of collision, plus a collision/ACK feedback
sum regret measured against the optimal orthogonal allocation of the U players to the U best channels
settings.definition_quote: Let $U\geq 1$ be the number of secondary users and $C\geq U$ be the number of orthogonal channels ... In each channel $i$ and slot $k$, the primary user transmits i.i.d. with probability $1-\mu_i>0$ ... We assume the collision model under which if two or more users transmit in the same channel then none of the transmissions go through.

settings.name_in_paper: Distributed learning and access under unknown number of users
unmapped: U <= C players, number of players U unknown but fixed; colliding transmissions all fail; no communication
each player observes channel availability plus collision feedback
sum regret against optimal orthogonal allocation to U best channels
settings.definition_quote: In this section, we consider the scenario, where the number of users $U$ is unknown (but fixed throughout the duration of transmissions and $U\leq C$, the number of channels).

algorithms.name: rho^RAND (distributed random allocation with g^MEAN statistic)
rho^EST (rho^RAND with collision-count estimation of number of users)

conditions: all channel means distinct and in (0,1)
self play: all users run rho^RAND
tuning: g^MEAN index: sample mean + sqrt(2 log n / T_{i,j}(n))

source.label: thm:randalloc
source.quote: The policy $\randalloc(U,C,\bfg^{\mbox{\tiny MEAN}} )$ in Algorithm~\ref{algo:randalloc} has $\Theta(\log n)$ regret.

results.notes: Paper states Theta(log n); proof only gives the upper bound by combining Prop. bounds, Lemma on U-worst time and collision theorem (constants depend on U, C, gaps and E[Upsilon(U,U)] <= binom(2U-1,U)-1). Regret defined via expected throughput with means, so pseudo-regret. Players are U = N, channels C = K.

conditions: self play: all users run rho^RAND

source.label: thm:intfrandalloc
source.quote: The expected number of collisions in the $U$-best channels under $\randalloc(U,C, \bfg^{\mbox{\tiny MEAN}} )$ scheme satisfies \beq \Ebb[M(n)] \leq U(\Ebb[\Upsilon(U,U)]+1)\,\Ebb[T'_j(n)].\eeq Hence ... $M(n) = O(\log n)$.

results.notes: Bound on expected number of collisions in the U-best channels, not regret.

conditions: each user has perfect knowledge of the channel means mu (no learning)

source.label: lemma:Pi
source.quote: The expected number of collisions under $\randalloc$ scheme in Algorithm~\ref{algo:randalloc}, assuming that each user has perfect knowledge of the mean channel availabilities $\mubf$, is given by \Ebb[M(n);\randalloc(U,C,\mubf)]\leq U\Ebb[\Upsilon(U,U)] \leq U\left[\binom{2U-1}{U}-1\right].

results.notes: Expected number of collisions under known means; N = number of users U.

symbols.xi_star: max_{k=1..U} xi(n;k), the maximum collision-count threshold, required to be omega(log n)

conditions: self play: all users run rho^EST
tuning: xi(n;k) = omega(log n) for all k > 1

source.quote: With threshold functions $\xi$ satisfying conditions in \eqref{eqn:cond_xi}, the policy $\unknownalloc(n,C,\statbf_j(m), \xi)$ in Algorithm~\ref{algo:unknownalloc} satisfies \limsup_{n \to \infty} \frac{R(n;\mubf, U, \unknownalloc)}{\xi^*(n;U)} <\infty.

results.notes: Hence O(f(n) log n) regret for any f(n) -> infinity. Horizon n is an input (doubling extension mentioned in footnote).
